name: codex-review
description: Dual-model code review: Claude staff-review + Codex adversarial review on any branch. Lightweight workflow for getting a thorough second opinion before pushing.

steps.name: setup

guards.message: No push until both reviews complete

steps.description: Identify the target: user provides a branch name, PR URL, or we use the current branch. Run git diff against the base branch (main/master) to understand the changeset. Save diff stats to .review/diff-summary.md.

steps.name: parallel-review
steps.description: Parallel dual-model review. FIRST: kick off /codex:adversarial-review --base main --background (fires Codex async, returns immediately). THEN: run /staff-review on the full diff. Save Claude findings to .review/claude-findings.md. AFTER staff-review completes: run /codex:result to collect Codex output. Save to .review/codex-findings.md. Both reviews run against the same diff, different models, different biases. If Codex is unavailable, proceed with Claude findings only.

steps.name: synthesize
steps.description: Merge Claude and Codex findings into a unified review. For each finding: note which model caught it (Claude, Codex, or both). Findings caught by both models are higher confidence. Deduplicate overlapping issues. Write final review to .review/unified-review.md with sections: (1) Agreement (both found it), (2) Claude-only findings, (3) Codex-only findings, (4) Recommended actions ranked by severity.

steps.name: fix-loop
steps.exit_condition: Zero CRITICAL or HIGH issues remain in the unified review. Tests pass.
steps.description: Address findings from the unified review, highest severity first. Run tests between each fix. If a Codex-only finding is ambiguous, use /codex:rescue to ask Codex to investigate further or propose a fix. Loop until no CRITICAL/HIGH remain.

steps.name: final-check
steps.description: Run the full test suite. Verify no regressions. Print a summary of what was fixed and what was accepted as-is. Changes remain local -- push decision is up to the user.
